To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we constructed linkage maps for the guppy using RAPD markers.

(1) the guppy genome is estimated to be approximately 4400 cM in size; (2) the sex-determinant region (Sd) is mapped on linkage group 3; (3) the sex-linked black tail (Bcp) gene is mapped on linkage groups 3 and 4; and (4) the sex-linked red tail (Rtd) gene is mapped onto linkage group 4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a linkage map for the guppy and the mapping of genes of economic importance.
the development of a genetic linkage map for the guppy, Poecilia reticulate, and with the identification of markers that may be linked to the sex-determinant region.
the development of molecular markers and the genetic linkage maps of the fish species Poecilia reticulate (Guppy).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic linkage map of the guppy is a very useful tool for the genetic analysis of this species, as well as for the other Poecilia species.
the linkage maps constructed for the Tuxedo × Wildtype cross and for the Wildtype × Tuxedo cross are both highly reliable, and that the maps are comparable.

the genetic linkage maps of the two independent guppy crosses are the first of their kind and are the first to provide a framework for the identification and mapping of QTLs for important traits in the guppy.

the linkage maps of the Tuxedo ⋅♂ ⋅♣ ⋅♀ × Wildtype ⋅♦ ⋅♀ cross and the Wildtype ⋆ ⋅♔ ⋆ ⫶ Tuxedo ⫶ ⫶ cross span 2100 Kosambe centiMorgels (cM) and 190 cM respectively, in 27 and 28 linkage groups respectively.
we were able to construct a genetic linkage map for the guppy (P. reticulata).
we have constructed the first genetic linkage maps of the Poecilia genus.
